long_biography.plain_text:
After a decade in lending, advertising and property development at Puget Sound Mutual Savings Bank, John W. Jacobi left to acquire an eight-agent brokerage in Seattle's Windermere neighbourhood. The move came during the region's early-1970s downturn, and Jacobi had no brokerage experience. He retained the office's agents and built a culture centred on professional autonomy and client relationships.

Growth came through additional Seattle offices and an affiliate network launched in 1984, extending Windermere across the western United States. Jacobi linked that expansion to local service, establishing an annual company-wide volunteer day and helping create a foundation funded through agents' commissions. He also founded the Windermere Cup rowing regatta. Long after leaving daily management, he returned to the University of Washington and completed the business degree he had begun six decades earlier.
